facts.statement: Bransonella was an extinct genus of marine xenacanth that lived during the Paleozoic era.
facts.quote: Bransonella is an extinct genus of marine xenacanth which lived during the Paleozoic era.

facts.statement: The teeth of Bransonella are small, measuring no more than 2 millimeters in size.
facts.quote: Teeth attributed to this genus are small, no greater than 2 millimeters.

facts.statement: Based on its small teeth, Bransonella likely had a body size not exceeding one meter in length.
facts.quote: This suggests a small body size likely not exceeding a meter in length.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Bransonella lived a lifestyle similar to modern catsharks, feeding on trilobites, crustaceans, gastropods, and occasionally small fish.
facts.quote: It has been suggested their lifestyle was similar to modern catsharks, eating trilobites, crustaceans, gastropods and occasionally small fish.

facts.statement: Bransonella belongs to the parent group Bransonelliformes.
Bransonella lived from the Tournaisian to the Roadian stages, between 358.86 and 266.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tournaisian to Roadian (358.86 to 266.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Bransonella was originally described by Harlton in 1933.
The first species described, B. tridentata, was initially misidentified as a conodont in 1933.
facts.quote: The first species described was B. tridentata in 1933, which was erroneously identified as a conodont.

facts.statement: B. nebraskensis has been found in the late Pennsylvanian of Nebraska and the middle Mississippian to early Permian of Kansas, the Urals, Poland, Belgium, Russia, and England.
facts.quote: B. nebraskensis was described from the late Pennsylvanian of Nebraska and later recognized from the middle Mississippian to the early Permian of Kansas, the Urals, Poland, Belgium, Russia, and England.

facts.statement: B. lingulata is known from the Serpukhovian stage of Russia.
facts.quote: B. lingulata is known from Serpukhovian of Russia.

facts.statement: B. tribula was described from the middle Permian Kaibab formation of Arizona.
facts.quote: B. tribula was described out of the middle Permian Kaibab formation of Arizona.

facts.statement: Additional fossils of Bransonella have been reported from the Mississippian of China and Australia, and the Pennsylvanian of Hungary and Brazil.
facts.quote: Additional reports of this genus come from the Mississippian of China and Australia as well as the Pennsylvanian of Hungary and Brazil.

facts.statement: Bransonella was used to establish a new order alongside Barbclabornia based on specific ornamentation features.
facts.quote: It was used to erect a new order along with Barbclabornia based on ornamentation.

rejected.statement: Bransonella is known only from its teeth, which feature cusp ornamentation shaped like an inverted 'V' and fin spines.
rejected.quote: It is known only from teeth which are easily distinguished from related genera by ornamentation on the cusp shaped like an inverted "V" and fin spines
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'shaped like an inverted V and fin spines'

rejected.statement: Bransonella is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
